options: Replaces the model with a search engine
Finds the passages relevant to the question, puts them in the prompt with ids, and asks the model to answer only from them with citations
Trains the model on your documents
explanation: Retrieval moves facts from the model's memory into the prompt, per request — the model supplies language and judgement, your documents supply facts.

stem: Fine-tuning is a poor way to add facts because…
options: It shifts behaviour reliably but knowledge unreliably, still invents specifics, and every fact change means retraining
explanation: Fine-tune for behaviour; retrieve for knowledge.

stem: Sending the whole corpus in every prompt instead of retrieving…
options: Costs tokens on every request, loses the middle of long prompts, and gives no citations
explanation: Long context is a capacity for one long document at low volume — not a retrieval strategy.

stem: The single feature only retrieval gives you for free is…
options: Provenance — a citation to the passage each claim came from
explanation: Citations let users check, reviewers audit, and code verify.

stem: Your knowledge changes daily. Which approach keeps answers current?
options: Retrieval — update the index, not the model
explanation: Freshness is an index update; fine-tuning is a training project.

stem: Most production systems end up with…
options: Prompting for rules + retrieval for facts, and fine-tuning only if evals show the prompt cannot get the behaviour
explanation: The approaches answer different questions; they combine.

stem: A cost RAG introduces that prompting alone does not…
options: An ingest pipeline, an embedding model and store, and two new failure modes that need their own metrics
explanation: Retrieval is engineering: pipelines, indexes and evals.

stem: Scoping the model to retrieved passages lets it…
options: Refuse when the documents do not cover the question instead of inventing an answer
explanation: The refusal path is one of the main things retrieval buys.

stem: The right case for long context rather than retrieval is…
options: A catalogue of a million products
One long document, low volume, high value — e.g. summarising a contract on demand
A support desk over a knowledge base
explanation: Capacity for one careful answer; not a retrieval strategy for traffic.

options: Must be rebuilt for every model release
Still works with next year's model — the documents and index outlive any vendor
Only works with the model that embedded it… for generation too
explanation: The embedding model must stay fixed for the index, but the generation model can change freely.
